Advances: ancora.derive

Stage: L7 part (b) (05a-stages-library.md; split per the refined plan decomposition note). Plan run dir on epic ancora-yzu.

Deliverable:
Ancora.Derive.DefIndex: module def/defp index, defaults expanded, parsed from source, symmetric on both sides; collects use forms for AR6. Ancora.Derive.Resolver: two-pass per-file resolution with ctx as pure data (membership predicate, ambient MapSet, def_index lookup); zero I/O and zero VM introspection inside; pass A collects imports at any depth including inside test blocks; pass B maintains the lexical alias stack; disposition table per ancora.derive.qualified_call_disposition, unqualified_ladder, dynamic_calls_unresolved (:dynamic_capture folded into :dynamic_module); parse options defaults plus emit_warnings: false. Ambient table construction (Kernel, Kernel.SpecialForms, ExUnit.{Case,Assertions,Callbacks,DocTest} exports) and rung 2b Code.ensure_loaded? + __info__ checks live in ctx construction in lib/ancora/derive.ex, not in the resolver; under --root the load path never includes the target _build.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: tagged_tests covering ancora.derive.qualified_call_disposition, unqualified_ladder, dynamic_calls_unresolved, resolver_is_pure, imports_and_aliases, parse_degrades_to_finding, formatter_round_trip (resolver half)
- Behaviors to demonstrate: ancora.derive.scenario.disposition_table_rows (one test per construct row, pure, async), import_inside_test_block, alias_stack_round_trip (stream_data), resolver_never_touches_io, unparseable_base_file (resolver half), own_corpus_round_trip (resolver half); real-shape fixtures: ConnCase-style with use-injected helpers, DataCase, for-comprehension test, macro DSL test, per-describe and per-test import
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale or named files plus mix spec.validate --root /Users/mz/src/ancora from specled_ex; no full suite mid-iteration
  - Final tier: the four common merge-gate commands run-until-green before IMPLEMENTED
  - Verifier tier: tagged tests for the ids above plus --stale only
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface: Resolver consumed by the Derive pipeline (L8 wires Task.async_stream over tagged test files); proving tests here are the disposition matrix
  - Fixture hygiene: fixture test files are source strings or tmp files, never compiled; resolver tests async
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable surface
  - Every conditional clause covered (every disposition row; each alias form; each unresolved kind)
- Call-site Integration: Ancora.Derive (ctx construction here, pipeline in L8) is the production caller of Resolver.resolve/3 and DefIndex; proving tests are the disposition matrix and the real-shape fixture suite.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/derive/{extract,compare,ack}.ex, lib/ancora/canonical.ex, lib/ancora/subject_files.ex (L8)
- lib/ancora/gate*, lib/ancora/output*, lib/mix/tasks/**
Allowed touches (this stage may modify):
- lib/ancora/derive/def_index.ex, lib/ancora/derive/resolver.ex, lib/ancora/derive.ex (ctx construction only)
- test/ancora/derive/{def_index,resolver,ctx}_test.exs, test/fixtures/resolver/**, test/support/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.derive.spec.md (acknowledging edits to requirement/scenario blocks only; never weakening)

Out of Scope (intent):
- no I/O, no ensure_loaded?, no Mix calls inside Resolver
- no resolution of apply with literal args; no guessing of dynamic calls
- no columns:, token_metadata:, or literal_encoder: parse options; no tolerant parser dependency

Merge gate:
- [ ] mix compile --warnings-as-errors
- [ ] mix test
- [ ] mix format --check-formatted
- [ ] mix deps.unlock --check-unused
- [ ] mix spec.validate --root /Users/mz/src/ancora passes (from specled_ex checkout)

- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

TEST_CRITIC: FAIL
Session: 68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-personal/projects/-Users-mz-src-ancora/68fab1f9-dfb5-49e0-be76-afa9d2d00f6d.jsonl

Blocking findings:

1. test/ancora/derive/resolver_test.exs:160-227 + test/fixtures/resolver/real_shapes.exs — no negative row for the DefIndex consultation on member imports. Mutation check: replace public_definition?/4 (lib/ancora/derive/resolver.ex:362) with `true` and the whole suite still passes. Every member-import test calls only signatures that are public in the index (helper/1, insert/1, route_path/1, assert_account/1); build_conn/0 in the fixture is rejected by the only: gates before the DefIndex gate is ever consulted. Real failure missed: under `import MyApp.Helpers`, a typo'd or private function call gets reported as a real binding {MyApp.Helpers, typo, n} instead of unresolved, poisoning the drift/growth/shrink sets. Needed row: import a member module (bare or with only: naming the call) whose DefIndex lacks/privates the function, assert kind :unqualified — and a second row for a member whose def_index returns :unknown.

2. test/ancora/derive/resolver_test.exs:160-184 — no negative row for only: REJECTING a signature. Mutation check: make import_admits? ignore only: entirely (lib/ancora/derive/resolver.ex:395) and the suite still passes — every falsely-admitted signature is then caught by the DefIndex gate instead (build_conn/0 is not public in any fixture index). except: has its rejection row (line 174); only: has only admission rows. Real failure missed: `import Mod, only: [x: 1]` followed by a call to public y/1 of Mod falsely binds to {Mod, :y, 1}. Needed row: import a member with only: excluding a signature that IS public in its DefIndex, assert unresolved. Findings 1+2 together mean either ladder gate can be silently broken today; only breaking both at once fails a test (real_shapes build_conn).

3. test/ancora/derive/resolver_test.exs:302-321 — the alias-stack property is trivial: `member_of(["Leaf", "Branch"])` is a 2-value domain interpolated into one fixed template, run 20 times. The scenario it is tagged to cover (ancora.derive.scenario.alias_stack_round_trip) calls for generated modules NESTING `alias ... as:`, `alias Foo.{Baz, Qux}`, and __MODULE__ frames around the call. Nothing here varies nesting depth, alias form, shadowing, or frame structure — it is two example tests wearing a property costume. Real failures missed: alias-through-alias chains deeper than one hop, grouped-alias targets used as prefixes, __MODULE__-prefixed aliases inside nested frames surviving the formatter round trip. Needed: a generator composing alias forms and nesting (e.g. bind over a list of frame constructors) that computes the expected module from the generated structure.

Notes (advisory):
- resolver_test.exs:324-330 purity-by-grep is a weak tripwire: a comment containing "IO." fails it; `:file.*`/`:os.*` erlang calls pass it. Fine to keep alongside the pure-ctx test at 333, but neither can actually detect impurity — worth acknowledging, not fixing.
- def_index_test.exs:35 and :53 spec tags look misattributed: nested-module indexing belongs to membership_source_derived, uses-collection to generated_bindings, not imports_and_aliases / qualified_call_disposition.
- resolver_test.exs:380 corpus test raises (rather than fails with a path) if any future repo file does not parse/format — an intentionally-broken fixture added later breaks it opaquely. Consider excluding fixtures or asserting parse first.
- No row for a bare `import Mod` (no options), and no row where an earlier admitting import misses and a later one resolves (source-order reduce_while continuation).

What is good: real lexical-scope negatives (sibling tests, case branches), each unresolved kind covered with file/line retention, both parse-degradation paths genuinely continue with derived/unparseable_source instead of raising, fixture stays an uncompiled source string, everything async, no sleeps, no VM-global state, no mirror logic in expectations.
